samples.summary: Sanitization lives in one store adapter, not at the engine boundary or in the NoteStore contract
samples.evidence: `sanitizeAuthor`/`sanitizeWrittenAt` are private to `packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts` (lines 50-68), but the only consumer of `getAuthorSpans()` is `packages/notes/src/view/blame-gutter.ts` (computeBlameLabels/authorOfRange), which happily renders whatever `author` string it is handed. The `NoteAuthorSpan` / `NoteStore.getAuthorSpans()` docs in store.ts:28-45 and 107-113 were NOT updated to state that implementations must return display-safe, past-clamped values, so the new invariant is enforced in exactly one implementation and silently bypassed by any other (MemNoteStore today, any future adapter tomorrow). The defensive step belongs at, or is at least mirrored at, the rendering boundary that the trust-boundary note itself calls the sole reader.

samples.summary: Third hand-rolled control/bidi stripper in the repo; no shared display-name sanitizer is reused
samples.evidence: `packages/backend/src/notification/notification.service.ts:42-57` already implements the same idea (`sanitizePreview`: strip zero-width/bidi, collapse C0/C1 controls, cap length) with a deliberately narrower character list and a documented rationale. The new `sanitizeAuthor` reimplements it with `/[\p{Cc}\p{Cf}]/gu` and its own cap, and nothing shared lives in `@wafflebase/core`. The repo's reuse expectation suggests one shared 'safe display string' helper rather than two divergent regexes whose behaviour differs (e.g. on U+2066-2069 vs the whole Cf class).

samples.summary: Trust-boundary hardening applied only to blame names; the identical unverified presence name shown on peer carets is left raw
samples.evidence: The new doc section and file header argue that a client-set presence `name` is an unverifiable claim and must be stripped of control/bidi characters and length-capped before display. `getPeerSelections()` (yorkie-note-store.ts:417-434) hands the very same `peer.presence.name` to the remote-caret label with no sanitization and no 'self-reported' qualification, so the stated boundary is only half-drawn. Pre-existing code, but this delta is what establishes the rule it violates.

samples.summary: Stripping the whole \p{Cf} class also removes legitimate joiners from real names
samples.evidence: `\p{Cf}` includes ZWJ (U+200D) and ZWNJ (U+200C), which are required in emoji ZWJ sequences and in correct Indic/Persian/Arabic orthography. The backend's equivalent (notification.service.ts:49) also strips them, but for a *display name* this can mangle a genuine user's name rather than only defusing a forged one; a narrower list (bidi overrides/isolates + zero-width spaces) would meet the stated goal with less collateral.
